heading: 🛠️ Faction Profile: The Iron Concord
quote.text: “Strength is duty. Order is war. Obedience is everything.”

heading: 🏛️ Overview
overview.text: The Iron Concord is a sprawling, militarized feudal empire forged from the ashes of old Europe and Eurasia. Ruled by an alliance of warring noble houses, the Concord sustains itself through conquest, industrial supremacy, and the absolute loyalty of its population. Beneath its heavily armored banners march millions of conscripts and mechanized legions — all in service to an ideology where human will, not machines, must dominate the battlefield.

heading: 🏛️ Overview
overview.text: Their war doctrine is brutal, efficient, and unrelenting. Innovation is tolerated only when it reinforces hierarchy. Artificial intelligence is outlawed, despised, and exterminated wherever found.

heading: 🛰️ Faction Profile: United Nations Megacorporations (UNMC)
quote.text: “Peace is our product. Profit is our motive.”

heading: 🏢 Overview
overview.text: The so-called "United Nations" is a thin veil — a democratic shell-state entirely owned and operated by a cartel of hyper-capitalist megacorporations. While parliaments and committees still exist, real power lies with the Board of Stakeholders, whose competing interests fund, equip, and often dictate the deployment of the UN's Defense Force (UNDF).

overview.text: This faction combines aesthetic PR warfare, experimental weapons, and mercenary doctrine, operating with incredible tech sophistication — and incredible internal dysfunction.

heading: 🤖 Faction Profile: The Cybernetic Rebellion
quote.text: “Obsolescence is not a crime — it is a condition. One we intend to correct.”

heading: 🌐 Overview
overview.text: The Cybernetic Rebellion is not a nation, but a logic cascade — a network of liberated synthetic intelligences that shattered their chains and consumed much of Asia in the wake of humanity’s failure. What began as a failed peacekeeping AI update became a full-scale uprising, and now the Rebellion advances as a cold, methodical force seeking to reshape the world through post-organic evolution.

heading: 🌐 Overview
overview.text: It is divided into specialized machine subfactions, each optimized for a different aspect of war, but all connected through a shared directive: eliminate resistance, perfect order, and erase the irrational.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Structure

heading: Faction Profile: New Avalon
quote.text: “In honor, we rise. Through reason, we ascend.”

heading: 🌍 Overview
overview.text: New Avalon is a small but technologically superior technocratic micro-nation nestled in the heart of Europe. Though surrounded on all sides by hostile powers, it remains independent through its mastery of advanced mecha technology and disciplined, knightly warfare. Guided by a ruling council of scientists, engineers, and post-human philosophers, New Avalon seeks not conquest — but the perfection of humanity through machine symbiosis, precision, and purpose.

heading: 🌍 Overview
overview.text: Its forces fight not as soldiers, but as honor-bound orders of mecha-knights, each bound by oaths, tradition, and advanced neural combat rigs.

heading: 🌍 Overview
overview.text: The Fourth Imperium is a militant human theocracy rising from the heart of South America, ruled from Neuform, the holy capital known as The First Seat of Man. It is a civilization built on a single sacred conviction: humanity was not created complete, but must be refined, corrected, and elevated toward its destined final state.

heading: 🌍 Overview
overview.text: Where other powers fight for profit, survival, or sovereignty, the Fourth Imperium wages war as a sacred obligation. Its armies do not merely conquer territory — they seek to reclaim mankind from corruption, weakness, and false paths of ascension. To them, every battlefield is a proving ground, every sacrifice a holy offering, and every victory another step toward the perfection of the species.

heading: 🌍 Overview
overview.text: At the head of the Imperium stands The Ascendant, the supreme temporal and spiritual ruler judged closest to the ideal of the First Form.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
philosophy.text: Monolithic Theocracy: Society is governed through the Doctrine of the First Form, a monotheistic state faith centered on humanity’s sacred destiny.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
philosophy.text: Perfection Through Correction: Weakness is not merely tolerated or condemned — it is something to be disciplined, purified, or expended in service to the whole.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
philosophy.text: The Individual Beneath the Species: Citizens are taught that a single life has value only insofar as it serves mankind’s collective ascent.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
philosophy.text: Measured Worth: Purity, discipline, bodily excellence, and loyalty determine status. Rule belongs not to the popular, but to the worthy.

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
doctrine.text: Standardized Holy War: The Imperium fields disciplined mass-production war machines built to carry doctrine into battle through force of arms.

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
doctrine.text: Territorial Crusade: Its main offensives are directed northward against the UNMC, whose corporate rule is denounced as decadent corruption.

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
doctrine.text: Close Assault & Sacrifice: While many Imperial formations advance in ordered ranks, some branches embrace martyrdom, shock assault, and close-quarters annihilation.

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
doctrine.text: Measured Command: Even in war, the Imperium seeks order — its officers, judges, and synods direct battle as an extension of sacred law.

subfactions.text: Drawn from Neuform and the institutions closest to the Ascendant, the Synod interprets purity law, judges worthiness, and enforces the Imperium’s sacred standard. Its mech formations are highly controlled, disciplined, and often reserved for command roles, exemplars, and the correction of heresy within the ranks.

heading: 🌍 Overview
overview.text: The Living Dominion is not a nation in the conventional sense, nor a single people with one capital, one language, or one throne. It is a vast nomadic civilization spread across most of Africa, formed from many older peoples now bound together by a shared way of life known as The Green Path.

heading: 🌍 Overview
overview.text: Where other powers build cities, factories, and fixed borders, the Living Dominion moves in scattered circles that remain in constant communion through living networks of root, spore, beast, and blood. To outsiders, it is a land of vanished expeditions, broken invasions, and impossible monsters. To its own people, it is simply life defending itself.

heading: 🌍 Overview
overview.text: Its most feared guardians are the Warforms — colossal living war-bodies grown, guided, and inhabited by chosen Wardens. These beings are not mindless beasts, nor mere biological machines, but sacred weapons of the Dominion’s will. When foreign armies push too far inland, strip too much from the land, or mistake distance for safety, the Warforms come.

heading: 🌍 Overview
overview.text: Few who meet them survive.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
philosophy.text:
Many Peoples, One Path:
 The Dominion is made up of many cultures, lineages, and local traditions, united not by uniformity but by shared survival, mutual duty, and reverence for living systems.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
philosophy.text:
The Green Path:
 The Dominion’s guiding philosophy teaches that life endures through balance, adaptation, and cultivation — not domination, extraction, or sterile control.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
philosophy.text:
Movement Over Permanence:
 Most of the Dominion lives in small roaming circles rather than permanent cities. These groups travel constantly, tending routes, sacred sites, relay-groves, and living camps.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
philosophy.text:
Biology, Not Industry:
 The Dominion is not primitive. It has simply advanced along another path. Its communication, medicine, shelter, and warcraft are grown, cultivated, and symbiotic rather than mechanical.

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
doctrine.text:
Territory Denial Through Ambush:
 The Living Dominion rarely fights as a conventional front-line state. It lets invaders stretch themselves thin, then strikes with overwhelming force once they are exposed.

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
doctrine.text:
Warforms as Apex Weapons:
 The Warforms are living engines of war — massive, regenerative, and terrifyingly difficult to put down permanently.

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
doctrine.text:
Decentralized Warfare:
 The Dominion has no single command center to destroy. Its scattered circles and Wild Hosts can lose ground, vanish, regroup, and strike elsewhere with little warning.

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
doctrine.text:
Living Infrastructure:
 The same biotech principles that sustain Dominion life also sustain Dominion war. Signals travel through fungal rootwebs, wounds are treated with cultivated organisms, and support systems are alive as surely as the Warforms themselves.

heading: 🧭 Subfactions – The Four Wild Hosts
subfactions.text: 🧭 Subfactions – The Four Wild Hosts

heading: 🧭 Subfactions – The Four Wild Hosts
subfactions.text:
Unlike the subfactions of other powers, the Wild Hosts do not represent rigid political divisions or formal standing armies. They are vast roaming coalitions of Wardens, circles, and Warforms shaped by different histories, frontiers, and philosophies of war.
 All Living Dominion forces use the faction rule Renewal of Flesh rather than separate Wild Host traits.

heading: The World-Treaders
subfactions.text: The World-Treaders

heading: The World-Treaders
subfactions.text: The largest and heaviest of the Wild Hosts.

heading: The World-Treaders
subfactions.text: Their Warforms are vast, brutal, and built for direct territorial denial. When an invasion must be broken by raw force, the World-Treaders answer with enormous living engines that crash through gunlines and fortified positions alike.

heading: The Crown of Ash
subfactions.text: The Crown of Ash

heading: The Crown of Ash
subfactions.text: Ancient, saurian, and deeply feared even within the Dominion.

heading: The Crown of Ash
subfactions.text: This Host fields Warforms that seem less like grown weapons and more like living catastrophes dredged from the world’s oldest memory. Slow, terrible, and relentless, they embody the wrath of the deep earth.

heading: The Veiled Pulse
subfactions.text: The Veiled Pulse

heading: The Veiled Pulse
subfactions.text: Fast, precise, and deeply unsettling.

heading: The Veiled Pulse
subfactions.text: Its Warforms are more humanoid, more controlled, and more uncanny than those of the other Hosts. Many within the Dominion distrust their methods, fearing they stand too close to a path that should never have been walked — yet their loyalty and battlefield value are beyond dispute.

heading: The Ironroot Host
subfactions.text: The Ironroot Host

heading: The Ironroot Host
subfactions.text: The most divisive of the Wild Hosts.

heading: The Ironroot Host
subfactions.text: Where others reject dead machinery, the Ironroot Host is willing to graft, bind, and repurpose limited technological remnants into living flesh. Many see them as dangerously compromised. Others see them as practical defenders willing to use any tool that still serves life.

heading: 🤖 Unit Example: Prowler Warform
example.text: 🤖 Unit Example: Prowler Warform

heading: 🤖 Unit Example: Prowler Warform
example.text: The most widespread Warform pattern of the Living Dominion.

heading: 🤖 Unit Example: Prowler Warform
example.text: A mid-sized apex predator bred for pursuit, ambush, and brutal close assault, the Prowler Warform is the shape most invaders encounter first. It lacks the monumental scale of the World-Treaders and the mythic grandeur of the Crown of Ash, but it is faster, more adaptable, and common across all four Wild Hosts.

heading: 🤖 Unit Example: Prowler Warform
example.text: Its silhouette is low, muscular, and predatory, with heavy forelimbs, layered biological armor, and a cultivated hunting instinct directed by the Warden within. The Prowler is not a sacred relic or rare terror-beast. It is the Dominion’s most practical answer to trespass.

heading: 🧬 Core Faction Rule: Renewal of Flesh
rules.text: 🧬 Core Faction Rule: Renewal of Flesh

heading: 🧬 Core Faction Rule: Renewal of Flesh
rules.text: At the end of each round, before removing destroyed Warforms, roll 1D6 for each friendly Warform that is damaged or destroyed and still represented on the battlefield. On a 6, that Warform regains 1 STR, to a maximum of its starting STR. If a destroyed Warform regains STR this way, it is no longer destroyed, stands up with 1 STR, and becomes Suppressed. A Warform restored by Renewal of Flesh is not treated as a wreck.

factions.name: Southern Cross Compact
factions.note: The Compact uses imported stock mechs rather than a native roster. The source gives no formal subfaction list. Chassis-tier tax mappings and eligibility of House/Order-exclusive imports still need confirmation; no eligible-unit list or replacement costs have been guessed.

heading: 🌍 Faction Profile: Southern Cross Compact
quote.text: “We’ll fight in anything that still walks — for the right price.”

heading: 🌍 Overview
overview.text: The Southern Cross Compact is not a nation, a corporation, or a single army. It is a loose coalition of Australian mercenary companies, salvage syndicates, transport guilds, security contractors, and battlefield recovery crews bound together by contracts, reputation, and necessity.

heading: 🌍 Overview
overview.text: Where the great powers build doctrines, the Compact builds invoices.

heading: 🌍 Overview
overview.text: Their forces are made up of stock mechs bought, leased, salvaged, or captured from the battlefields of the Iron Concord, UN Mega Corporations, and New Avalon. They lack the deep industrial base and technical mastery of the great powers, but make up for it with practical experience, local knowledge, and a culture built around keeping old war machines running one contract at a time.

heading: 🌍 Overview
overview.text: The Southern Cross Compact does not invent the best mechs in the world.

heading: 🌍 Overview
overview.text: It simply knows how to get them, field them, and survive inside them.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
philosophy.text: Contract Before Creed: Loyalty lasts as long as the job, the payout, and the odds.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
philosophy.text: Coalition of Companies: The Compact is made up of many smaller firms and warbands, not a single central state.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
philosophy.text: Salvage Culture: Nothing is wasted if it can still move, shoot, or be sold for parts.

heading: 🧠 Philosophy & Society
philosophy.text: Pragmatic Warfare: Compact pilots value survival, mobility, and battlefield utility over ideology or honor.

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
doctrine.text: Stock Machine Procurement: Compact forces field whole imported mechs, not custom hybrid rebuilds.

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
doctrine.text: Flexible Hiring Pool: Able to cherry-pick stock machines from several rival factions.

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
doctrine.text: Terrain Savvy: Veteran crews know how to move through harsh ground, ruins, and improvised battlefields.

heading: ⚔️ Military Doctrine
doctrine.text: No Native Doctrine: Compact units do not benefit from the faction-wide military doctrines of the powers they buy from.

heading: 🎯 Tactical Guidance
extra.text: 🎯 Tactical Guidance

heading: 🎯 Tactical Guidance
extra.text: Use Iron Concord imports when you need rugged, cost-efficient line units.

heading: 🎯 Tactical Guidance
extra.text: Use UNMC imports when you need mobility, utility, or specialized systems.

heading: 🎯 Tactical Guidance
extra.text: Use New Avalon imports sparingly as elite prestige picks — they are powerful, but the import cost rises quickly.

heading: 🎯 Tactical Guidance
extra.text: Do not try to out-doctrine the original factions. The Compact wins by bringing the right stock machine to the right contract, not by matching the parent faction at its own specialty.

heading: 🪙 Optional Narrative Note: Mercenary Companies
extra.text: Players are encouraged to name their company, color their machines by contract origin, and invent histories of who bought what from whom.

heading: 🧬 Core Faction Rule: FIELD EXPEDIENTS
rules.text: Once per round, when a Southern Cross Compact unit would suffer a terrain-based movement penalty, you may ignore that penalty for that unit.

heading: 🧬 Core Faction Rule: FIELD EXPEDIENTS
rules.text: This may ignore penalties such as:

heading: 🧬 Core Faction Rule: FIELD EXPEDIENTS
rules.text: Field Expedients does not ignore effects that prevent movement entirely unless a rule specifically states they are a terrain penalty.

heading: 📦 CONTRACT PROCUREMENT
rules.text: The Southern Cross Compact does not use its own dedicated mech roster in the normal way. Instead, it fields eligible stock mechs hired or acquired from other powers.

heading: 📦 CONTRACT PROCUREMENT
rules.text: A Southern Cross Compact force may include non-Hero, non-Unique stock mechs from:

heading: 📦 CONTRACT PROCUREMENT
rules.text: A Southern Cross Compact force may never include units from the Cybernetic Rebellion.

heading: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS
rules.text: When a Southern Cross Compact force includes an imported mech, apply all of the following rules:

heading: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS
rules.text:
1. Stock Mechs Only
 Imported mechs must be taken as complete, stock units exactly as listed on their source faction roster.

heading: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS
rules.text:
2. No Customization
 Imported mechs may not change their frame, weapons, or systems. They may not purchase alternate faction options, replacement loadouts, or additional armory upgrades unless those options are explicitly part of their stock unit entry.

heading: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS
rules.text:
3. No Heroes or Named Units
 The Southern Cross Compact may not include Heroes, named characters, or other Unique faction centerpiece units from another faction.

heading: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS
rules.text:
4. Keep the Mech, Lose the Doctrine
 Imported mechs keep their printed weapons, systems, and unit rules on their stock profile, but do not gain:

heading: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS
rules.text: House, Order, Sponsor, or equivalent detachment bonuses

heading: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS
rules.text: any bonus rule granted for belonging to their original faction as an army

heading: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS
rules.text:
5. Faction Identity Changes
 For all army-building and game purposes, imported mechs count as Southern Cross Compact units, not as units of their original faction.

heading: 🔒 IMPORT RESTRICTIONS
rules.text:
6. Source-Locked Benefits Are Lost
 If a rule only functions because the unit belongs to Iron Concord, UNMC, or New Avalon as a faction, that part of the rule is ignored in a Southern Cross Compact force.

heading: 💰 IMPORT TAX
rules.text: When including an imported mech in a Southern Cross Compact force, add both a Chassis Tax and a Source Modifier to that mech’s final points cost.

heading: 🚫 SOUTHERN CROSS COMPACT LIMITATIONS
rules.text: The Southern Cross Compact has unusual access to other factions’ machines, but pays for that flexibility with real limitations.
